test_cases.title: Verify user registration with valid details
test_cases.resolution_summary: This test case requires a user registration flow that does NOT exist in the AURA framework. The AURA framework is designed for HP Instant Ink enrollment flows with HPID authentication, not generic user registration. The framework has HPIDPage for HP ID account creation (which includes firstName, lastName, email, password fields), but NO HomePage, RegistrationPage, or ConfirmationPage as described in the test case. All page objects, helpers, and locators for the generic registration flow described in this test case need to be created from scratch.

critical_gaps: AURA framework is designed for HP Instant Ink enrollment flows, NOT generic user registration
No HomePage exists - AURA uses LandingPage for HP Instant Ink landing page
No generic RegistrationPage exists - AURA uses HPIDPage for HP ID account creation (different from generic registration)
No registration confirmation page exists - AURA has ConfirmationPage for enrollment order review, not user registration success
All page objects (HomePage, RegistrationPage, ConfirmationPage/RegistrationSuccessPage) must be created from scratch
All locators for these pages must be created from scratch
All methods for these pages must be created from scratch
HPIDPage can serve as a reference template since it has similar fields (firstName, lastName, email, password, create_account_button)
test_cases.automation_notes: This test case requires creating an entirely new registration flow that does not exist in the AURA framework. The framework is purpose-built for HP Instant Ink enrollment with HPID authentication. To automate this test case, developers must create: (1) HomePage page object with home_page_container and register_button locators, (2) RegistrationPage page object with all form field locators (username, email, password, confirm_password, first_name, last_name, submit_button), (3) ConfirmationPage or RegistrationSuccessPage for success message verification, (4) All corresponding methods for navigation, form filling, and verification. The HPIDPage can serve as a reference template since it has similar registration fields. Estimated development effort: 3-5 days for a developer familiar with the AURA framework.

summary.notes: The test case describes a generic user registration flow that does NOT exist in the AURA framework. AURA is purpose-built for HP Instant Ink enrollment with HPID authentication. Only infrastructure files (base classes, browser management, test utilities) exist. All page objects, locators, and methods for HomePage, RegistrationPage, and ConfirmationPage must be created from scratch. HPIDPage can serve as a reference template.
